This modest birth mass is characteristic of primates that exhibit a relatively altricial developmental pattern despite their precocial locomotor abilities. Capuchins are born with their eyes open and a well-developed grip, yet they remain almost entirely dependent on maternal transport and nursing during the first several weeks of life. This pronounced sex difference in maturation timing is unusual among New World monkeys and has been linked to the species' complex social system, where young males must attain sufficient body size and social rank before successfully competing for mating opportunities.
